The live line says what its first time measures
## Today

`foedrum brew`'s live line starts with the batch's time since its order, as a bare number (`liveLine`, `src/cli/brew.ts`; ADR 0179):

```
- 34m 22s / gauge #1 / 53s / turn 12 / Edit test/integration/demo-la
```

In the self-brew trial (#374) a person read that as "this step has run for 34 minutes", when `gauge #1` had run for 53 seconds. The batch's age includes every earlier stop and wait, so it can be far from what is running now.

## What to build

- [ ] The live line says what that first time measures, in one or two short words, for example `ordered 34m 22s ago / gauge #1 / 53s / …`. Choose the words, and keep the attempts' fields as they are.
- [ ] A batch with no recorded order time, which counts from this brew's start, says that instead, truthfully: it must not claim an order time it does not have.
- [ ] The line is still cut to the terminal's width, with the attempts' fields kept as far as they fit.

**See it:** the live line of `foedrum brew` on a terminal, or the output of the tests in `test/unit/brew-live-line.test.ts`.

For the self-brew trial (#374): small on purpose. If it changes what ADR 0179 says, a new ADR amends it. An existing Brewery needs no migration.
